context.exploration_scope: Independently re-verified PHASE-SSI-S1's 2 CANDIDATE_ONLY improvement signals against the current canonical Experience Layer, current E12/E23/E33/S-series registries, and each signal's own real/simulated action linkage

problem: PHASE-SSI-S1 found 2 CANDIDATE_ONLY improvement signals but explicitly did not validate, adopt, or apply either -- it was unverified whether those 2 signals' evidence still held up, were still non-duplicate, and were still tied to real (not simulated) project actions once independently re-checked.

decision.decision_summary: 2 CANDIDATE_ONLY signal(s) from S1 re-checked. 1 passed evidence-existence, fresh re-grouping equality, non-duplication, and real-linkage re-verification (VALIDATED_CANDIDATE): sig_goal_production_runtime_successful_resolution. 1 rejected on recheck. 0 automatic adoption, 0 rule-ization, 0 real project modifications. Verdict: VALIDATED_SIGNAL_FOUND.

action.action_summary: Re-verified each of S1's CANDIDATE_ONLY signals: confirmed every evidence_ref still exists, recomputed the (goal_ref, experience_kind) grouping fresh and required an exact member-set match, re-ran S1's own E12/E23/E33+S-series duplication check, and checked every evidence record's action.real_or_simulated field for real linkage.

result.note: 1 signal(s) independently re-verified and classified VALIDATED_CANDIDATE -- still not applied, not auto-adopted, not rule-ized.

cause.root_cause_summary: A CANDIDATE_ONLY signal from one phase is a snapshot, not a standing fact -- without an independent re-check in a later phase, evidence drift, duplication against something registered since, or accidental reliance on simulated (not real) actions could all pass silently into an eventual real adoption decision.

lesson: Validating a candidate signal means re-deriving its evidence from scratch and re-running the same non-duplication checks independently, not re-reading the prior phase's own verdict -- a signal that still holds up under a fresh, independent recomputation is meaningfully stronger evidence than one that was merely asserted once.
